quotes.text: Where the metres drilled on a day cross a band boundary, the metres in each band are charged as a separate charge stating the depths at which that part starts and ends. A boundary depth belongs to the shallower band. Bands end at 1,500 m, 3,000 m and 4,500 m.
Item PD-210 is charged at the rate for the band in which the metres lie (Clause 23). A boundary depth belongs to the shallower band.
Band 1 0 m to 1,500 m 42.35 / Band 2 over 1,500 m to 3,000 m 58.15 / Band 3 over 3,000 m to 4,500 m 76.45 / Band 4 over 4,500 m 98.70

The rate for item PD-210 is taken at the percentage below according to the metres already drilled on the well in the Contract Year (Clause 3A). Metres are counted from zero at the start of each Contract Year, and an interval that crosses a band is divided at the band.
The rate is class-rated under Schedule 3 Part 2 and is not section-rated.
The first Contract Year runs from the Commencement Date to the day before its first anniversary, and each following Contract Year from that anniversary.
The well-class factor in Schedule 3 Part 2 is not applied to item PD-210, Schedule 2 having already priced the metre by depth.
Charges on an HPHT well, showing a Standby day, the circulating-hour minimum not engaged, and footage split at a band boundary.
Class-rated services: DD-120, PD-210, MW-310, MW-320, LW-410, LW-411, LW-412, LW-413.

discrepancies: No unsupported claim. Checks: App B (p30, not among the cited pages) prints 2,930-3,000 x 70 at 58.15 = 4,070.50 and 3,000-3,085 x 85 at 76.45 = 6,498.25 (both correct); these are the unfactored Band 2/Band 3 rates on an HPHT well (HPHT factor 1.325, Sch 3 Part 2 p20), consistent with 17B. Ambiguity (not resolved): Sch 2 p17 note says the PD-210 rate 'is class-rated under Schedule 3 Part 2' and Sch 3 Part 2 (p20) lists PD-210 as class-rated, which with Cl.18 would apply the class factor; 17B (p35) says the well-class factor is not applied to PD-210. The rule follows 17B and App B. Also, Sch 2 Part 2 bands are '1 m to 40,000 m' / '40,001 m to 120,000 m' / 'above 120,000 m' (integer metres; how fractional metres or 0 m are placed is not stated).

quotes.text: A service Schedule 3 Part 3 marks as not chargeable is not charged on a Standby day in any quantity.
On a Standby day item DD-120 is not charged and item DD-121 is charged instead.
The percentage of the operating rate charged on a Standby day (Clause 20). Services charged per well or for a loss are charged in full whatever the status of the day.
DD-120 Rotary steerable system, circulating Not chargeable
DD-121 is charged only on a Standby day, in place of item DD-120 (Clause 21).
The Company may suspend the services on any well. A day of suspension recorded as Standby on the Daily Drilling Report is charged under Clause 20.
A day lost to weather is recorded as Standby on the Daily Drilling Report.

discrepancies: No unsupported claim. Label note: the heading '13. Suspension' is printed at the foot of p3; its operative text is on p4, so 'Cl.13 (p4)' is acceptable. Sch 3 Part 3 (the Standby table) runs from p20 to p21 and Part 4 is on p21, consistent with 'Sch 3 Parts 3-4 (pp20-21)'. Validation 'DD-120 on a Standby day' follows from Cl.20/Cl.21 and the 'Not chargeable' entry; 'DD-121 on an Operating day' follows from Part 4 ('charged only on a Standby day'). The per-well / loss items (DD-140, LW-430, MB-701, MB-702, LH items) do not appear in the Part 3 table; the full-charge statement in the Part 3 lead-in covers them.

quotes.text: No service is charged on any day in a quantity above the daily limit in Schedule 3 Part 5.
Part 5 — Daily limits
DD-101 Directional driller, 24-hour coverage 2 person-day
HC-640 Cuttings bed monitoring 1 day

discrepancies: Cl.22 limits the quantity charged 'on any day'; it does not say 'per well'. The title's 'per well per day' adds a per-well qualifier the text does not state (the text is silent on whether the limit is per well or per day across all wells; the literal words read as per day). 'Across invoices' is consistent with 'on any day' (the clause limits the quantity charged on the day, not per invoice) but is not stated in terms. Scope '22 limited services' is correct: Sch 3 Part 5 lists 15 codes on p21 (DD-101, DD-102, DD-110, DD-120, DD-121, DD-130, PD-201, PD-220, PD-230, MW-301, MW-310, MW-320, MW-330, LW-401, LW-413) and 7 on p22 (RM-511, RM-520, RM-530, HC-601, HC-610, HC-620, HC-640). Validation 'DD-101 x3 on one day' exceeds the printed limit of 2 person-day by 1.

quotes.text: Item DD-111 is charged once for each BHA run carrying a positive displacement motor, on the last day of that run. Item LW-420 is charged once for each BHA run carrying a radioactive source, on the first day of that run.

Items MB-701 and DD-140 are charged once for the well, on the first day on the well. Items LW-430 and MB-702 are charged once for the well, on the last day on the well; item LW-430 only where logging while drilling was run.
Gyro surveys, formation pressure points, wiper trips, back-reaming hours and clean-out runs are charged in the numbers recorded on the Daily Drilling Report for an Operating day.
Part 6 — Charges once per well DD-140, LW-430, MB-701, MB-702 (Clause 27).
DD-111 Motor redress and inspection each BHA run, as Clause 26 describes
DD-140 Well planning and anti-collision study once for the well, as Clause 27 describes
LW-420 Radioactive source handling each BHA run, as Clause 26 describes
HC-630 Casing drift and clean-out run each BHA run, as Clause 26 describes
MB-702 Demobilisation from rig site once for the well, as Clause 27 describes
B BHA run record: run number, first and last day of the run, tools in the run, circulating hours, metres logged and reamed, and whether a radioactive source was carried every day of a run
D Radioactive source handling: the sources handled and their certification a day on which a source was run
A charge for a service below is not payable until the part named has been completed in the Daily Drilling Report for the day or run the charge is for (Clause 37).
DD-111 Motor redress and inspection Daily Drilling Report, Part B
LW-420 Radioactive source handling Daily Drilling Report, Part D

discrepancies: No unsupported claim about DD-111, LW-420, MB-701, MB-702, DD-140 or LW-430. Validation: Part B is completed 'every day of a run' and records the first and last day of the run, while Cl.26 charges DD-111 'once for each BHA run ... on the last day of that run', so repeated Part B entries do not create a second DD-111; LW-420 requires Part D ('the sources handled and their certification'). Ambiguity (not resolved): 'HC-630 per Q5' cites Q5, which is not a contract provision and cannot be checked against the scan. Sch 8 (p28) charges HC-630 'each BHA run, as Clause 26 describes', but Cl.26 names only DD-111 and LW-420 and gives no day for HC-630, while Cl.30 (p7) charges 'clean-out runs ... in the numbers recorded on the Daily Drilling Report for an Operating day'. The text does not settle on which day of a run HC-630 falls. Whether a Part D that is present but lacks certification counts as 'completed' is also not stated.

quotes.text: No service is charged twice for the same well and the same day, save that item PD-210 may be charged more than once on a day for different depth intervals under Clause 23.
Where the metres drilled on a day cross a band boundary, the metres in each band are charged as a separate charge stating the depths at which that part starts and ends.

discrepancies: No unsupported claim. The validation case 'MDS-00164-050 wrong-day report is not a duplicate' names an invoice/record reference that is not in the contract and cannot be checked against the scan; it is consistent with Cl.29 applying to 'the same well and the same day'. Ambiguity (not resolved): Cl.29 allows more than one PD-210 on a day 'for different depth intervals under Clause 23', and Cl.23 provides for separate charges only where the day's metres 'cross a band boundary'. The text does not say whether two non-overlapping PD-210 intervals within one band on one day are permitted, nor expressly how partly overlapping intervals are treated (the rule reads overlap as not 'different depth intervals').

quotes.text: Where a tool cannot be recovered, the charge is its replacement value in Schedule 6 less depreciation of 1 per cent for each complete 25 circulating hours the tool accumulated on the well, as stated on the Lost in Hole Report, to a depreciation of not more than 50 per cent. The result is rounded under Clause 17 and charged as one unit on the day of the loss.

The replacement values in Schedule 2D are stated in SAR and are converted into the currency of the Contract at the rate of exchange published in that Schedule for the month in which the tool was lost, rounded half to even, before the depreciation in Clause 31 is applied. Schedule 6 states the same values in the currency of the Contract as they stood when it was let, and Schedule 2D governs.
The tools were bought in riyals and the values below are stated in SAR. They are converted into the currency of the Contract under Clause 31A at the rate published for the month of the loss.
Rate of exchange, as published:
Depreciation is 1 per cent for each complete 25 circulating hours, to not more than 50 per cent (Clause 31).
Circulating hours for Clause 31 are those the tool accumulated on the well on which it was lost, including the day of the loss.
With 412 hours the depreciation under Clause 31 is 16 per cent.

discrepancies: No unsupported claim. Arithmetic: 412/25 = 16.48 -> 16 complete blocks -> 16% (matches App F p34); 24 h -> 0 complete blocks -> 0%; 25 h -> 1%; 1,250/25 = 50 -> 50%, which is the printed maximum ('not more than 50 per cent'). Parameter DDS.P.lih_depreciation matches Cl.31 and the Sch 6 note. Notes: the Sch 2D exchange table is headed 'Halalas per USD'; none of the four printed SAR values divided by any of the 24 printed monthly rates gives an exact half cent, so the 'half cent' validation case is a constructed test, consistent with 31A 'rounded half to even'. Cl.31 takes hours 'as stated on the Lost in Hole Report', while Sch 5 (p24, not cited) says there are no separate loss documents and the hours are in DDR Part E; the rule does not depend on this.

quotes.text: No service is charged for a day on which the rig is moving between wells; such days are not days on the well.
A day lost to weather is recorded as Standby on the Daily Drilling Report.
Where a tool fails in the hole, the day remains an Operating day for the other services; the failed tool is charged only on days the report records it in the hole.
No uplift is payable for work at night; the rates in Schedule 1 cover continuous operations.
No uplift is payable for work on a public holiday.

discrepancies: No unsupported claim. P4 supports the validation case 'service on a rig-move day' (no service is charged). Note: P6 does not make a day non-chargeable; it keeps the day Operating for other services and limits the failed tool's charge to days the report records it in the hole. The title groups it under 'days not chargeable or not uplifted' without misstating it.

quotes.text: Item PD-210 is charged only on the performance-drilled sections nominated in the call-off.
Performance-drilled section a 12-1/4 inch or 8-1/2 inch section of a well the call-off nominates for performance drilling.

discrepancies: No unsupported claim. The validation case (PD-210 outside the 12-1/4 / 8-1/2 sections) follows from the App A definition. Note: the definition requires both the size (12-1/4 or 8-1/2 inch) and nomination by the call-off, so a 12-1/4 or 8-1/2 inch section the call-off does not nominate is also excluded. The call-off is not part of the scanned contract, so which sections are nominated for a given well cannot be read from the scan.

quotes.text: The net amount of an invoice is the sum of the amounts of its charges, including the discount charge under Clause 38.

Where the sum of the amounts of the services charged on an invoice exceeds 250,000.00 USD, the Contractor allows a discount of 4 per cent of the excess, rounded under Clause 17, stated as a single charge under code DS-900 with a negative amount.
Value Added Tax is charged at 15 per cent of the net amount of the invoice, rounded under Clause 17.
The total of an invoice is its net amount plus Value Added Tax.
The discount under Clause 38 is calculated on each invoice alone and not on the Contractor's invoices taken together.
Net amount (below the discount threshold) 25,662.26
Value Added Tax at 15 per cent 3,849.34
Invoice total 29,511.60
On an invoice whose services total 312,400.00, the discount charge under Clause 38 is -2,496.00.

discrepancies: No unsupported claim. Arithmetic: App B lines 2,955.76 + 2,975.75 + 9,162.00 + 4,070.50 + 6,498.25 = 25,662.26; 15% x 25,662.26 = 3,849.339 -> 3,849.34; 25,662.26 + 3,849.34 = 29,511.60. (312,400.00 - 250,000.00) x 4% = 2,496.00 -> -2,496.00. Exactly 250,000.00 does not 'exceed' 250,000.00, so no discount. Parameters: threshold printed '250,000.00 USD', discount '4 per cent', VAT '15 per cent'. 'Half-even' rests on 'rounded under Clause 17' in Cl.38 and Cl.39; Cl.17 (p6, not cited) sets the half-to-even rule, worded for the steps of the Clause 18 build-up. The validation case 'correction crossing the threshold' is not addressed in terms by the text.

quotes.text: Reference DDS-2025-118/A3. Issued 17 August 2026 and taking effect 1 February 2026.

Services performed on or after that date and already invoiced shall be re-priced at the substituted rates and the difference shown as a single adjustment on the first invoice submitted after the date of issue (Clause 36A).
DD-120 Rotary steerable system, circula hour 398.50 416.00 2026-02-01
DD-101 Directional driller, 24-hour cov person-day 1,916.50 1,954.00 2026-02-01

Where this instrument and an earlier instrument both state a rate or a discount for the same service, the later governs services performed on or after its effective date, and the earlier governs services performed before it.

Where an Amendment substitutes a rate with effect from a date before the date it was issued, an invoice submitted before that date of issue was correct at the rate then in force. The difference on services already invoiced is shown as a single adjustment on the first invoice submitted on or after the date of issue, and on no other.
Each takes effect on its own effective date and governs services performed on or after it; nothing in an instrument reopens a service already charged at the rate then chargeable.
The Contractor shall invoice each well separately, for a period of consecutive days on the well.

discrepancies: No unsupported claim. The statement correctly reports that 36A says 'on or after the date of issue' and A3 says 'after the date of issue' (issue date 17 August 2026), so an invoice submitted 2026-08-17 qualifies under 36A but not under A3's wording. Scope 'DD-120, DD-101 services from 2026-02-01' matches the A3 table and the SoV row. Ambiguities (not resolved): (1) 36A/A3 vs Cl.32: invoices are per well, and the text does not say whether 'the first invoice submitted' means the first invoice for the same well or the first invoice on the Contract. (2) The SoV lead-in says 'nothing in an instrument reopens a service already charged at the rate then chargeable', while A3 requires already-invoiced services to be 're-priced' through a single adjustment. (3) Supplement No. 2 (effective 2026-04-01) and Amendment No. 2 (effective 2026-07-01), both issued before A3, also state a rate or a percentage for DD-120/DD-101. A3's 'later governs' sentence does not say whether 'later' means later issued or later effective, so it is open how far after 2026-04-01 the A3 rates govern. (4) Nothing in the text addresses how the adjustment interacts with the DS-900 base ('services charged on an invoice') or with VAT.
